lead: Bending forms a sheet along a straight line without deliberately changing its thickness. The flat blank is not simply the sum of the outside dimensions. The bend consumes an arc of neutral-axis length called the bend allowance; for a 90° bend the flat length is the sum of outside dimensions minus the bend deduction. Springback, the elastic recovery after the punch lifts, makes the final angle open up, so the tool must overbend or bottom the sheet. Bending makes brackets, enclosures, car panels and appliance bodies. A shop cutting a blank for a UPI payment terminal enclosure uses this calculation before the first cut.
prereq: You need 3.1 for ductility and 3.2 for blank edges.

sections.h3: Bend line, radius and neutral axis

blocks.text: Bending is a forming operation. A straight bend line divides the sheet. The punch pushes the sheet into a die. Material inside the bend compresses; material outside stretches. The neutral axis is the surface that neither stretches nor compresses. Its position is K × t from the inside surface. Here t is sheet thickness in mm, and K is the K-factor, a dimensionless number usually between 0.33 and 0.50. A common estimate for mild steel is K = 0.40. The inside bend radius R is measured in mm on the inner surface. The bend angle θ is the angle through which the sheet turns, in degrees. A 90° V-bend has θ = 90°.
The bend allowance BA is the arc length of the neutral axis. It is the length of sheet consumed by one bend.

blocks.where: BA is the bend allowance in mm; θ is the bend angle in degrees; R is the inside bend radius in mm; K is the K-factor; t is the sheet thickness in mm. The factor π/180 converts degrees to radians. The quantity R + Kt is the radius of the neutral axis.

blocks.text: For θ = 90°, R = 4.0 mm, t = 2.0 mm and K = 0.40, BA = 7.54 mm. This number goes into the flat blank.

The flat blank length is the sum of the straight lengths plus one bend allowance for each bend. Do not use the outside radius R + t in place of R + Kt. The neutral axis lies inside the outer surface, so the outside radius overestimates the arc length.

For a 90° bend, the outside setback is OSSB = R + t. The bend deduction is BD = 2(R + t) − BA. Here BD is in mm, R is inside radius, t is thickness, and BA is bend allowance. The flat length can also be found as the sum of outside dimensions minus BD. For the same 90° bend, R = 4.0 mm, t = 2.0 mm and BA = 7.54 mm, so BD = 2(4.0 + 2.0) − 7.54 = 4.46 mm.

If the bend line is too near the sheet edge, the outer fibre has little material to hold it. The edge cracks or tears. Keep the bend line a few thicknesses away from the edge. The exact clearance depends on ductility and is checked by trial.

Springback is elastic recovery after the punch is removed. The bent part does not keep the full punch angle; it opens slightly. Springback increases with high yield strength, small thickness and large bend radius. A high-strength steel bracket springs back more than a soft mild steel bracket of the same shape.

Compensation uses overbending or bottoming. With θ as the turn angle, overbending sets the punch to a larger turn angle than the final turn angle. If a 90° turn springs back by 2°, set the punch to 92° turn (92° − 2° = 90°). If a shop quotes the included angle between flanges instead, that is the angle 180° − θ; for the same case set 88° included to finish at 90° included. Bottoming presses the sheet against the die bottom at the end of the stroke; the through-thickness plastic strain reduces springback. Stretch bending also reduces it by keeping the sheet in tension.

The minimum bend radius is the smallest inside radius that avoids cracking on the outer surface. A smaller R means a sharper bend and a larger outer-fibre strain. Ductile sheet can bend to about its own thickness; less ductile sheet needs a larger radius. Edge cracking is different from centre cracking: it starts at the free edge when the bend line is too close.

V-bending uses a V-shaped die. The sheet rests on two shoulders, and the punch descends into the V. The punch depth sets the bend angle. V-bending is common on a press brake and can make different angles with the same die.

Edge bending clamps the sheet and bends a flange over the die edge. It makes long straight flanges, such as the side of an enclosure. The clamp holds the sheet flat while the punch bends only the projecting edge.

Roll bending passes the sheet through three rolls. The middle roll is offset, so the sheet takes a large-radius curve. It makes cylindrical shells, tanks and pipe sections. Roll bending gives a continuous curvature, not a single sharp bend.
Figure 1 shows the V-bending mechanism. The punch presses the 2.0 mm sheet into the die; the punch is set past 90° turn so the bent part finishes near 90° turn after springback.

examples.question: A 2.0 mm thick mild steel sheet is bent to 90° with an inside bend radius of 4.0 mm. Take K = 0.40. (a) Find the neutral-axis offset Kt in mm. (b) Find the bend allowance BA in mm. (c) For this 90° bend, find the bend deduction BD = 2(R + t) − BA in mm.
steps: Write the data: t = 2.0 mm, R = 4.0 mm, θ = 90°, K = 0.40.
examples.answer: Kt = 0.80 mm, BA = 7.54 mm, and BD = 4.46 mm.
examples.check:
import math
t = 2.0
R = 4.0
K = 0.40
theta_deg = 90.0
Kt = K * t
BA = (math.pi / 180.0) * theta_deg * (R + Kt)
BD = 2.0 * (R + t) - BA
print(f"{Kt:.2f}")
print(f"{BA:.2f}")
print(f"{BD:.2f}")

traps: Using the outside radius R + t in the bend allowance instead of the neutral-axis radius R + Kt.
Forgetting K or setting K = 0.50 for every material; K depends on material and R/t and usually lies between 0.33 and 0.50.
Mixing bend allowance with bend deduction: BA is added to straight lengths, while BD is subtracted from the sum of outside dimensions.
Treating springback as a bend allowance error. Springback changes the final angle after unloading; compensate by overbending or bottoming.
Putting the bend line too close to the sheet edge, which causes edge cracking before the bend reaches full angle.

quiz.a: Bend allowance is the arc length of the neutral axis through the bend, in mm. It is the length of sheet consumed by the bend and is added to the flat blank.

quiz.q: What is the usual range of the K-factor?
quiz.a: The K-factor usually lies between 0.33 and 0.50. It gives the neutral-axis position as a fraction of sheet thickness from the inside surface.

quiz.q: Why does springback increase with high yield strength?
quiz.a: A high yield strength means the material resists plastic deformation and stores more elastic strain. When the punch is removed, this elastic strain recovers, so the bend opens up more.

quiz.q: Give one difference between V-bending and edge bending.
quiz.a: V-bending presses the sheet into a V-die and sets the angle by punch depth. Edge bending clamps the sheet and bends only a projecting flange over the die edge.

quiz.q: A 1.5 mm sheet is bent to 60° with inside radius 3.0 mm. Take K = 0.45. Find the bend allowance.
A 90° bend is made with R = 5.0 mm and t = 2.0 mm. Take K = 0.40. Find BA.
With θ as the turn angle, a 90° turn springs back by 2° after the punch lifts. What punch turn angle should be set to get a final 90° turn, and why? State the included-angle setting too.
quiz.a: Set the punch to 92° turn. The part springs back by 2° of turn during elastic recovery, so 92° − 2° = 90° final turn. This is overbending. In the included-angle convention between flanges, the same setting is 88° included, because included angle = 180° − turn angle.

beyond: Not for the exam. Modern press brakes use CNC and laser angle measurement to correct springback automatically. Finite element models of bending predict the neutral-axis shift for high-strength steels. Search for bend deduction charts, K-factor tables and press-brake springback compensation.
